headline: PM sets September deadline for second Padma and Jamuna bridges
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has instructed officials to complete feasibility studies for new crossings over the two major rivers by next year.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has ordered officials to complete feasibility studies for the construction of second bridges over the Padma and Jamuna rivers by September next year.
The Prime Minister issued these directives during a meeting with officials from relevant ministries and divisions on Tuesday afternoon.
The proposed second Padma bridge is expected to feature a Y-shaped design to improve connectivity.
The second Jamuna bridge will prioritize transport connectivity to the northern region, including Rangpur.
Additionally, the Prime Minister has directed authorities to move forward with the construction plans for the Padma Barrage project.
Once the feasibility assessments conclude in September, final decisions will be made regarding the locations, designs, and project costs of both bridges.
caption:
Two new major bridges are coming. The PM has set a September deadline for feasibility studies on second Padma and Jamuna crossings.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has ordered officials to complete feasibility studies for the construction of second bridges over the Padma and Jamuna rivers by September next year.

The Prime Minister issued these directives during a meeting with officials from relevant ministries and divisions on Tuesday afternoon.

The proposed second Padma bridge is expected to feature a Y-shaped design to improve connectivity.

The second Jamuna bridge will prioritize transport connectivity to the northern region, including Rangpur.

Additionally, the Prime Minister has directed authorities to move forward with the construction plans for the Padma Barrage project.

Once the feasibility assessments conclude in September, final decisions will be made regarding the locations, designs, and project costs of both bridges.

headline_marked: Police fire teargas as [[garment workers clash with police]] in Mirpur-11
headline: Police fire teargas as garment workers clash with police in Mirpur-11
summary: Protests over minimum wage demands enter their fourth day, leading to clashes in Dhaka's Mirpur-11 area as police use teargas and sound grenades to disperse crowds.
details: RMG workers in Dhaka's Mirpur-11 clashed with police today after attempting to take to the streets to protest for a higher minimum wage.
The unrest began around 10:30am when workers walked out of several factories and gathered in alleys on the western side of Mirpur-11, attempting to reach the main road.

Police, who were already on alert, chased the workers, who responded by hurling brickbats. The clashes continued for nearly half an hour before police fired teargas shells and sound grenades to force a retreat.
Following the clash, members of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal took positions on the main road, claiming they were there to prevent sabotage by infiltrated Awami League members.

Touhidul Arif, deputy commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Public Order Management division, stated that 'miscreants with ulterior motives' were involved in the unrest rather than actual workers.
The protests over minimum wage demands have now entered their fourth consecutive day, with similar unrest reported in Savar, Ashulia, and Narayanganj.
caption:
Police used teargas and sound grenades to disperse garment workers in Mirpur-11 as wage protests enter their fourth day.

RMG workers in Dhaka's Mirpur-11 clashed with police today after attempting to take to the streets to protest for a higher minimum wage.

The unrest began around 10:30am when workers walked out of several factories and gathered in alleys on the western side of Mirpur-11, attempting to reach the main road.

Police, who were already on alert, chased the workers, who responded by hurling brickbats. The clashes continued for nearly half an hour before police fired teargas shells and sound grenades to force a retreat.

Following the clash, members of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal took positions on the main road, claiming they were there to prevent sabotage by infiltrated Awami League members.

Touhidul Arif, deputy commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Public Order Management division, stated that 'miscreants with ulterior motives' were involved in the unrest rather than actual workers.

The protests over minimum wage demands have now entered their fourth consecutive day, with similar unrest reported in Savar, Ashulia, and Narayanganj.
